title: Finite etale neighbourhood realization of a map of completions
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $D$ a finite type commutative $A$-algebra, and $R$ a commutative Noetherian $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume that $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $\widehat D=\varprojlim_nD/I^nD$ and $\widehat R=\varprojlim_nR/I^nR$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For every $A$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:\widehat D\to\widehat R$, there exist a commutative etale finitely presented $R$-algebra $R'$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], with structural map $j:R\to R'$, and an $A$-algebra map $u:D\to R'$ such that $j$ induces an isomorphism $R/IR\xrightarrow{\sim}R'/IR'$ and $\widehat u=\widehat j\circ\varphi$ as maps $\widehat D\to\widehat {R'}$. No henselian-pair hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ (lemma-fully-faithful-etale-over-complement), existence and final finite-etale-neighbourhood factorization assertion; etale finitely presented means an affine etale algebra.

proof.text: Put $J=IR$ and let $\eta:R\to H=R^h$ be the henselization of $(R,J)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], $(H,JH)$ is henselian and $H$ is the filtered colimit of the etale $R$-algebras $R_\lambda$ inducing an isomorphism modulo $J$. Take a small skeleton of this essentially small category. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion], $H$ is Noetherian and $\eta$ induces the canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:\widehat R\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat H$. Composing $\varphi$ with $\theta$, apply [lem-per-etale-away-completion-hom-lifting] to the original $A,I,D$ and the Noetherian henselian $A$-algebra $H$. This gives an $A$-algebra map $w:D\to H$ with $\widehat w=\theta\varphi$. The extended ideal is $IH=JH$, so the completions in that application are exactly these.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ (lemma-fully-faithful-etale-over-complement), statement and first proof paragraph; henselian specialization followed by Tag 0AGV

proof.text: Since $A$ is Noetherian and $D$ is of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes $D$ finitely presented over $A$. Regard the small filtered diagram of Step 1 as a diagram of $A$-algebras through $A\to R$. Its colimit in rings is $H$, with $A$-algebra coprojections. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] with base ring $A$, source $D$ and map $w$. Obtain an etale $R$-algebra $R'$ in this diagram and $u:D\to R'$ over $A$ such that $ku=w$, where $k:R'\to H$ is its coprojection. Its structural map $j:R\to R'$ has $kj=\eta$ and induces $R/IR\cong R'/IR'$ by the definition of the diagram. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization](1), $R'$ is finitely presented over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ, first proof paragraph, final-assertion argument; Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization) and Tag 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation)

proof.text: The etale map $j$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers] gives isomorphisms $j_n:R/J^n\to R'/J^nR'$ for every $n\ge1$. These are the quotient maps of $j$, so they commute with reduction between powers. Taking compatible sequences, [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-completion-data] identifies $\widehat j:\widehat R\to\widehat {R'}$ as an isomorphism. This is the canonical completion map, not an arbitrary isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat), proof for each etale stage, and Tag 0AGV (lemma-henselization-Noetherian-pair), completion comparison

proof.text: Completion acts on maps componentwise on the quotients. Therefore $kj=\eta$ gives $\widehat k\widehat j=\theta$, and $ku=w$ gives $\widehat k\widehat u=\widehat w=\theta\varphi$. Both $\widehat j$ and $\theta$ are isomorphisms, so $\widehat k=\theta(\widehat j)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Cancel it in $\widehat k\widehat u=\widehat k\widehat j\varphi$ to obtain $\widehat u=\widehat j\varphi$. Together with Step 2 this is every required clause.
